overview: Students have the opportunity to experience high-quality dental education, modern clinical facilities, research opportunities and a strong focus on preventive and community oral healthcare in Denmark. In Denmark, the dental education pathway is integrated into a 3-year Bachelor’s in Odontology followed by a 2-year Master’s in Odontology (approx. 5 years total). Clinical training, patient assessment, and evidence-based oral health promotion are core components. Note that the majority of qualifying dentistry programs are taught in Danish, requiring language proficiency alongside strong academic credentials in biology and chemistry.

universities.name: University of Copenhagen
universities.desc: Provides university education and research in odontology. Its academic environment comprises research, scientific study and education related to dental and oral health, associated with clinical dentistry.

universities.name: Aarhus University
universities.desc: Offers dental education and research through its dental-related academic programs. Students can explore its academic information to understand the program structure, teaching language and admission conditions.

faq.question: What is the length of study for Dentistry in Denmark?
faq.answer: The university route usually takes about five years, split between a three-year bachelor's degree and a two-year master's degree in odontology.

faq.question: Are dentistry courses in Denmark conducted in English?
faq.answer: Many qualifying programs in dentistry are taught in Danish. Check with the university for the language of instruction and the required Danish language proficiency before applying.

faq.question: Can Indian students study dentistry in Denmark?
faq.answer: Yes, if they meet the university's academic, language and other admission requirements. Indian applicants should check the qualification assessment, subject prerequisites and language requirements for the program they intend to apply for. Dentistry in Denmark for Indian students requires careful planning, particularly when reviewing language and qualification conditions.

faq.question: What is the cost of living in Denmark as a student?
faq.answer: A planning estimate is ₹90,000–₹1,40,000 per month, depending on your accommodation and lifestyle. Tuition fees, travel, insurance and other initial expenses should be budgeted for separately.

faq.question: Are international graduates allowed to work as dentists in Denmark?
faq.answer: They must fulfil the relevant Danish professional authorization and language requirements. Graduates are advised to consult the appropriate authority (Danish Patient Safety Authority - Styrelsen for Patientsikkerhed) to understand the current rules before undertaking professional practice.
